proofs.proof_tex:
The exact-primitives proposition gives
\[
 \kappa(c^\dagger)=\frac58.
 \tag{3}
\]
By the Airy-benchmark definition and the declared condition \(C_A\in(0,\infty)\),
\[
 \Lambda_{c^\dagger}
 =C_A\kappa(c^\dagger)^{2/3}
 =C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\in(0,\infty).
 \tag{4}
\]
The effective normalized Airy-record lemma ensures that every spline record used by the corrected diagonal is produced by a terminating rational interval procedure and has normalized energy at most \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+2^{-k_n}\).  Hence no oracle for an arbitrary real number is being used.  Conclusion \({\rm(C)}\) of the allocation-tube theorem supplies admissibility
\[
 \alpha_n(3T_{k_n}^\dagger+2\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A})\le1
 \tag{5}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), as well as the four nonnegative errors and the computable nonincreasing tail \(E\).

Fix such an \(n\).  The exact-primitives proposition identifies the target under the corrected response-count prior as
\[
 \tau_{c^\dagger}(m)
 =\frac1n\sum_t m_t(c^\dagger)^\top t,
 \tag{6}
\]
which is the response-count representation of the same finite-population causal contrast \(\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\), not a surrogate estimand.  By \((5)\), the corrected permutation-orbit Bayes lemma applies.  For every outcome-independent assignment law \(\mathcal D_n\) and every possibly randomized labeled-data estimator, it bounds the Bayes risk below by
\[
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\pi(r)
 \mathcal B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
 \ge
 B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A},
 \tag{7}
\]
where \(\pi\) is the allocation-count law induced by \(\mathcal D_n\).  Maximum risk dominates Bayes risk.  Taking the infimum over precisely the designs and estimators in \(\mathrm{def:risk\text{-}game}\) therefore yields
\[
 R_n(c^\dagger)
 \ge B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}.
 \tag{8}
\]
This is also the lower inequality returned at each admissible fixed input by the corrected fixed-input evaluator lemma.

By \(\mathrm{def:exact\text{-}airy\text{-}tube\text{-}bayes\text{-}risk}\), the allocation set is finite and nonempty and
\[
\begin{aligned}
 n^{4/3}\left\{\frac1n-
 B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\right\}
 &=n^{4/3}\left\{\frac1n-
 \min_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
 \mathcal B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\right\}\\
 &=\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
 G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r).
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
The local, positive-count exterior, and zero-count sets in conclusion \({\rm(A)}\) partition \(\mathcal R_{n,3}\).  Applying the corresponding line of \({\rm(A)}\) on each member of that partition gives
\[
 \max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}
 G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)
 \le \Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-.
 \tag{10}
\]
Combining \((9)\) and \((10)\), and dividing by the positive number \(n^{4/3}\), gives
\[
 B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
 \ge \frac1n-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-\}n^{-4/3}.
 \tag{11}
\]
Equations \((8)\) and \((11)\) prove the first two inequalities in \((1)\).

Conclusion \({\rm(B)}\) supplies a total finite procedure \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) with
\[
 \max_y\mathbb E\!\left[
 \{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
 \right]
 \le \frac1n-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}n^{-4/3}.
 \tag{12}
\]
Because its outcome-independent design and total estimator are feasible actions in \(\mathrm{def:risk\text{-}game}\), the infimum defining \(R_n(c^\dagger)\) is no larger than the left side of \((12)\).  This proves the last two inequalities in \((1)\).  Independently, the rational-grid primal-error lemma proves that the corrected finite procedure can be chosen with
\[
 e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
 \le (B_{c^\dagger}+1/4)n^{-1/6}+2^{-n},
 \tag{13}
\]
so the attaining side is a genuine total finite-data construction.

Subtracting the two risk bounds in \((1)\) from \(n^{-1}\) and multiplying by \(n^{4/3}>0\) gives the squeeze
\[
 \Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
 \le n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
 \le \Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-.
 \tag{14}
\]
Conclusion \({\rm(C)}\) says that, for every \(n\ge N\), each of the four errors in \((14)\) is at most \(E(N)\).  Hence \((14)\) implies \((2)\).  Given any \(\eta>0\), computable monotone convergence of \(E\) supplies an \(N\) for which \(E(N)<\eta\); then \((2)\) holds for all \(n\ge N\).  Therefore
\[
 n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
 \longrightarrow \Lambda_{c^\dagger}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Rearranging \((15)\) gives the asserted risk expansion, and \((4)\) proves that its coefficient is finite and strictly positive.  The proof uses conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\) of the allocation-tube theorem and does not prove those conclusions themselves.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), let \(k_n\), the verified spline record, \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\), \(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), and \(E\) be the outputs in conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\) of \(\mathrm{thm:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}allocation\text{-}tube}\), and put
\[
 e_n^- = \max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\}.
\]
For every sufficiently large \(n\), the corrected exact Bayes certificate and the total finite procedure \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) output by that theorem satisfy
\[
 \frac1n-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-\}n^{-4/3}
 \le B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
 \le R_n(c^\dagger)
 \le \max_{y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}}
       \mathbb E\!\left[
       \{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
       \right]
 \le \frac1n-\{\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}n^{-4/3}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The Bayes inequality in \((1)\) is valid against every outcome-independent, possibly dependent assignment law and every randomized labeled-data estimator.  For every \(N\) beyond the finite startup of the diagonal and every \(n\ge N\),
\[
 \left|n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
       -\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\right|\le E(N),
 \qquad E(N)\downarrow0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}n^{-4/3}
 +o(n^{-4/3}),
 \qquad
 \Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\in(0,\infty).
\]

proposed.justification: This node isolates the exact effective corollary of the corrected all-count bridge: its two finite inequalities and common tail imply the sharp unrestricted decision value at the designated unequal contrast.
proposed.gap: The corollary itself is proved here, but its load-bearing allocation-tube dependency remains open; in particular, no direct argument in this node establishes the uniform local, exterior, or zero-face bounds.
proposed.consumer: Once the allocation-tube root is proved, the displayed squeeze gives a sharp worst-case precision benchmark for a fixed-horizon three-regimen trial using the \(1:-1/4:-3/4\) contrast.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The dependency spine must point directly to the corrected allocation-tube theorem, normalized Airy record, corrected fixed-input evaluator, and rational-grid primal certificate, with no widening-prior object or error ledger.

prose_updates.tldr: For \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\), the proved sharp result is currently the fixed-independent-design expansion with coefficient \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}=C_A(5/8)^{2/3}\), together with the corresponding one-sided lower limit for the unrestricted deficit. The former widening polynomial tube is exactly refuted. Its replacement is an effective compact rational Airy spline-square prior: a rational interval ODE/Taylor oracle certifies normalized energy and weighted tails, and a fixed-input evaluator computes exact ordered-field Bayes intervals and finite allocation-stratum maxima. The sharp-limit and effective-certificate nodes are now faithful corollaries of the corrected allocation-tube conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\); because that all-count bridge remains open, the unrestricted sharp equality is not yet established.

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent proves the \(n^{-4/3}\) order and finite response-type programs, while the proved fixed-independent theorem identifies the Airy coefficient. No available result gives the reverse inequality for every outcome-independent dependent design. The missing step is a uniform corrected-prior Bayes bridge covering \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation perturbations, all positive-count exterior allocations, and zero-count faces with one effective remainder.
project_justification.niche: At \(c^\dagger\), all eight response types and a nonzero transverse nuisance direction are needed because a scalar-path prior can be exploited by a pair-focused design. The scientifically meaningful unresolved question is whether unrestricted designs improve on the fixed allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\) at second order.
project_justification.fill: The current verified contribution gives the exact response-alphabet geometry, a total fixed-independent Airy procedure, an effective normalized rational Airy-record algorithm, a genuine corrected transverse prior at every admissible input, an exact permutation-orbit Bayes reduction, and a terminating same-input ordered-algebraic evaluator. The proposed root theorem states the precise all-count inequalities, four certified errors, and monotone tail certificate still needed; its dependent sharp-limit and effective-certificate nodes now expose only the consequences of those corrected conclusions.

sampling_model.design: The causal game permits every outcome-independent assignment law, including dependence across labeled units and zero allocation to an arm. The proved comparator assigns units independently with \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\). The corrected prior is selected independently of the design, and the orbit reduction is exact at every fixed allocation count; uniform optimization over all counts remains open.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap condition is imposed on the unrestricted design. Positive local counts, positive exterior counts, and zero-count faces are separate required conclusions of the corrected bridge, so boundary allocations cannot be discarded by assumption.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no superpopulation nuisance estimation. The compact transverse coordinate is a design-independent prior device orthogonal to the finite-population contrast; shrinking it while retaining uniform control of posterior denominators and allocation boundaries is part of the open proof.

prose_updates.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) provide the scalar two-arm Airy benchmark and feedback bounds, not a three-active-arm all-design converse. Hull (2026) is likewise a two-arm unrestricted result. The accepted parent supplies the exact finite orbit game, first-order value, second-order order, and same-sample rational certificate sandwiches. The present verified machinery gives the effective normalized rational Airy record, exact corrected tube prior, permutation-orbit Bayes reduction, and same-input evaluator; it does not supply the uniform all-count asymptotic bridge. Hirano and Porter (2009) and Levit (1986) inform the limiting decision and spectral architecture. Bai (2023), Armstrong (2022), and Aronow and Lopatto (2026) concern related randomization or allocation restrictions but do not settle this unrestricted second-order game. Hammer et al. (1996) supplies only the prospective complete binary-endpoint regimen-trial motivation; no censored-outcome reanalysis is claimed.
prose_updates.interpretation: A prospective trialist can use the proved fixed-independent allocation \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\), its total Airy-feedback estimator, and the terminating same-input certificate machinery for the finite-population contrast. The reauthored sharp-limit theorem shows exactly how the corrected Bayes certificate, four errors, and computable tail would yield an unrestricted sharp benchmark. Until the allocation-tube root is proved, that conditional squeeze must not be presented as evidence that dependent designs have no second-order advantage.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(K=3,n=3\) full-label risk \(511653/4000000\) is below the scalar Bayes lower value \(18213/136000\), but this does not establish an asymptotic gap. A longitudinal-only prior is defeated by a pair-focused design, and the former widening polynomial prior is refuted by its exact Bayes-risk calculation. The rational Airy replacement fixes normalized longitudinal energy measured through the quotient and is effective at every fixed input, but finite enumeration cannot prove a common future-sample tail. The remaining task is a likelihood or Bayes-information expansion uniform over local counts, exterior shells, posterior denominators, and zero-count faces. Published comparator; no novelty claimed: for support two, direct evaluation gives \(\kappa(c)=1\) and the published two-arm coefficient \(C_A\).
prose_updates.honest_scope: The root bridge is confined to \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) with fixed three-arm support. Unconditionally proved results include the fixed-independent expansion with coefficient \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\), its total finite procedure, the one-sided unrestricted lower limit, the effective normalized Airy-record algorithm, and fixed-input corrected Bayes and primal certificates. The unrestricted sharp equality and its cross-sample effective certificate remain dependent on the open allocation-tube conclusions. No growing-arm, uniform vanishing-weight, or arbitrary-real computability claim is made, and equality versus strict second-order loss for the independent design remains unresolved.

statement_notes.justification: This node is the equation-by-equation effective corollary of conclusions \({\rm(A)}\)--\({\rm(C)}\): the corrected Bayes certificate and total procedure squeeze the deficit around \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\).
statement_notes.gap: The corollary has no separate mathematical gap, but it inherits the still-open allocation-tube theorem and therefore does not make the unrestricted equality unconditional.
statement_notes.consumer: After the root bridge closes, it supplies the sharp worst-case precision benchmark for the designated fixed-horizon three-regimen contrast.

proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(n\) be in the admissible tail supplied by the unequal-three-arm allocation-tube theorem.  The effective normalized Airy-record lemma proves that the spline record selected at \(k_n\) is produced after finitely many rational interval operations.  The allocation-tube theorem gives
\[
\alpha_n\{3T_{k_n}^\dagger+2\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\}\le1, \tag{1}
\]
so the positivity premise of the corrected finite-input evaluator holds.  Apply that evaluator with \(\delta_n=n^{-3}\).  Its conclusion gives rationals \(b_n^-\le b_n^+\), a rational feasible grid value \(U_n\), and a total estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) under \(q^\dagger\), with
\[
\begin{aligned}
b_n^-&\le B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\le b_n^+,\\
b_n^+-b_n^-&\le n^{-3},\\
b_n^-&\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le
\max_y\mathbb E\!\left[
\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
\right]\le U_n.
\end{aligned} \tag{2}
\]
Here the lower inequality against \(R_n(c^\dagger)\) is an all-procedure statement: by the corrected permutation-orbit calculation built into the finite-input evaluator, the maximum risk of every outcome-independent design and every randomized labeled-data estimator dominates the Bayes risk \(B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\), and the infimum in the risk-game definition preserves that inequality.  The upper inequality in (2) is witnessed by the displayed total estimator.  The rational-grid primal-error lemma verifies that this finite grid program is the attaining certificate used by the corrected diagonal machine and that its primal error is effective.

We next derive the upper bound on the unrestricted scaled deficit from the three allocation regions; it is not assumed.  Abbreviate
\[
\mathcal B_n(r)=
\mathcal B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r),
\qquad
G_n(r)=G_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r).
\]
By the exact Airy-tube Bayes-risk definition, the finiteness of \(\mathcal R_{n,3}\), and the fact that multiplication by the positive number \(n^{4/3}\) reverses a minimum after subtraction from \(n^{-1}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}-
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\right\}
&=n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}-\min_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}\mathcal B_n(r)\right\}\\
&=\max_{r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}}G_n(r). 
\end{aligned} \tag{3}
\]
The local positive-count set, the positive-count exterior set, and the zero-count set in conclusion (A) of the allocation-tube theorem are disjoint and cover \(\mathcal R_{n,3}\).  Applying its corresponding bound on each set to (3) therefore gives
\[
n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}-
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\right\}
\le \Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-,
\quad
e_n^-=\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\}.
\tag{4}
\]
Since (2) also gives
\(R_n(c^\dagger)\ge
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\), equations (3)--(4) imply
\[
D_n=n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-.
\tag{5}
\]

The finite lower endpoint has only the requested algebraic-enclosure loss.  Indeed, (2) implies
\[
0\le
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}-b_n^-
\le b_n^+-b_n^-\le n^{-3}. \tag{6}
\]
Using (3), (4), and (6),
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_n^+
&=n^{4/3}\left\{n^{-1}-
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\right\}
+n^{4/3}\left\{
B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}-b_n^-\right\}\\
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-+n^{4/3}n^{-3}\\
&=\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-+n^{-5/3}\\
&\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-+n^{-1}.
\end{aligned} \tag{7}
\]
The inequality \(R_n(c^\dagger)\ge b_n^-\) in (2) also gives \(D_n\le d_n^+\).

For the opposite side, let \(U_{\Lambda,n}\) be the rational upper endpoint for \(\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\) in the verified diagonal record.  The evaluator-handle definition gives
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}\le U_{\Lambda,n},
\qquad
\left[n^{4/3}(U_n-n^{-1})+U_{\Lambda,n}\right]_+
\le e_{\mathrm{pr},n}. \tag{8}
\]
For every real \(z\), \(z\le[z]_+\).  Hence (8) yields
\[
n^{4/3}(U_n-n^{-1})+\Lambda_{c^\dagger}
\le e_{\mathrm{pr},n},
\]
or equivalently
\[
d_n^-=n^{4/3}(n^{-1}-U_n)
\ge\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}. \tag{9}
\]
Because \(R_n(c^\dagger)\le U_n\) by (2), multiplication by \(-n^{4/3}<0\) and addition of \(n^{1/3}\) give \(d_n^-\le D_n\).  Combining (5), (7), and (9) proves all displayed finite-sample inequalities.

It remains to prove effectiveness across sample sizes.  Conclusion (C) of the allocation-tube theorem supplies a code and correctness certificate for a rational-valued nonincreasing computable \(E\) with \(E(N)\to0\) and
\[
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},
e_{\mathrm{zero},n},e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}\le E(N)
\qquad(n\ge N). \tag{10}
\]
Thus \(F(N)=E(N)+1/N\) is rational-valued, nonincreasing, computable, and tends to zero.  Given rational \(\eta>0\), enumerate \(N=1,2,\ldots\), replaying the finite tail certificate from conclusion (C), until
\[
F(N)=E(N)+1/N\le\eta. \tag{11}
\]
The certified convergence of \(E\) makes this search terminate; call the first accepted tail index \(N^\dagger(\eta)\).  For \(n\ge N^\dagger(\eta)\), equations (5), (7), (9), and (10) give
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-E(N)\le d_n^-\le D_n
\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+E(N),
\qquad
D_n\le d_n^+\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+E(N)+1/N. \tag{12}
\]
The first chain in (12) also gives \(d_n^-\le\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+E(N)\), while the two chains together give \(d_n^+\ge\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-E(N)\).  Therefore (11)--(12) prove the three asserted absolute-error bounds and the enclosing relation \(d_n^-\le D_n\le d_n^+\).

Finally, diagonal mode is total by the evaluator-handle definition.  Before it certifies (1), its flag identifies the finite exceptional prefix.  On such an input, choose the outcome-independent allocation \(q^\dagger\) and the deterministic estimator zero.  Since \(\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\in[-1,1]\), its squared error is at most one, while squared-error risk is nonnegative.  Hence \(0\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le1\), proving the stated safe prefix certificate.  Every operation used here has integer, rational, or ordered-algebraic input, so no representation of an arbitrary real contrast is required.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Fix \(c=c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\).  Run the diagonal Turing machine furnished by the unequal-three-arm allocation-tube theorem, and write its outputs as \(k_n\), the verified record for \(\varphi_{k_n}^\dagger\), \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\), \(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), and \(E\).  This machine terminates on every input.  Its admissibility flag is positive for every sufficiently large \(n\), and then
\[
\alpha_n\{3T_{k_n}^\dagger+2\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\}\le 1.
\]
Put \(\delta_n=n^{-3}\).  At every such admissible input, finite-input mode of \(\mathsf E\) terminates and returns rationals \(b_n^-\le b_n^+\), an exact rational worst-case-risk certificate \(U_n\), and a total randomized estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) under the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\), such that
\[
b_n^-\le B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\le b_n^+,
\qquad b_n^+-b_n^-\le\delta_n,
\qquad
b_n^-\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le
\max_y\mathbb E\!\left[
\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
\right]\le U_n.
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
e_n^-&=\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\},\\
D_n&=n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\},\\
d_n^-&=n^{4/3}(n^{-1}-U_n),
\qquad
d_n^+=n^{4/3}(n^{-1}-b_n^-).
\end{aligned}
\]
The returned finite certificates verify
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le d_n^-\le D_n\le
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-,
\qquad
D_n\le d_n^+\le
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-+n^{-1}.
\]
The same machine returns a code and proof certificate for a rational-valued nonincreasing computable function \(E\) satisfying \(E(N)\to0\) and
\[
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},
e_{\mathrm{zero},n},e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}\le E(N)
\qquad(n\ge N).
\]
Consequently, for every rational \(\eta>0\), a terminating search returns a computable \(N^\dagger(\eta)\) such that, for all \(n\ge N^\dagger(\eta)\),
\[
d_n^-\le D_n\le d_n^+,
\qquad
|d_n^--\Lambda_{c^\dagger}|\le\eta,
\qquad
|D_n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}|\le\eta,
\qquad
|d_n^+-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}|\le\eta.
\]
On the finite inadmissible prefix, the evaluator returns its flag and the deterministic zero estimator with the valid bracket \(0\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le1\); hence the finite-data procedure is total for every \(n\).  No computability representation of an arbitrary real contrast is used.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen claim uses the refuted widening-polynomial prior, fixed widening schedules, and an obsolete error ledger that are not conclusions of the corrected Airy machine. The replacement drops those unsupported objects and narrows the theorem to the exact corrected Airy diagonal, its four certified errors, and the computable common tail supplied by the unchanged allocation-tube root.

proposed.statement:
Fix \(c=c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\).  Run the diagonal Turing machine furnished by the unequal-three-arm allocation-tube theorem, and write its outputs as \(k_n\), the verified record for \(\varphi_{k_n}^\dagger\), \(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\), \(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\), and \(E\).  This machine terminates on every input.  Its admissibility flag is positive for every sufficiently large \(n\), and then
\[
\alpha_n\{3T_{k_n}^\dagger+2\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}\}\le 1.
\]
Put \(\delta_n=n^{-3}\).  At every such admissible input, finite-input mode of \(\mathsf E\) terminates and returns rationals \(b_n^-\le b_n^+\), an exact rational worst-case-risk certificate \(U_n\), and a total randomized estimator \(\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}\) under the independent allocation \(q^\dagger\), such that
\[
b_n^-\le B_{n,k_n,\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm A}}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}
\le b_n^+,
\qquad b_n^+-b_n^-\le\delta_n,
\qquad
b_n^-\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le
\max_y\mathbb E\!\left[
\{\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm A}-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2
\right]\le U_n.
\]
Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
e_n^-&=\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\},\\
D_n&=n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\},\\
d_n^-&=n^{4/3}(n^{-1}-U_n),
\qquad
d_n^+=n^{4/3}(n^{-1}-b_n^-).
\end{aligned}
\]
The returned finite certificates verify
\[
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}-e_{\mathrm{pr},n}
\le d_n^-\le D_n\le
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-,
\qquad
D_n\le d_n^+\le
\Lambda_{c^\dagger}+e_n^-+n^{-1}.
\]
The same machine returns a code and proof certificate for a rational-valued nonincreasing computable function \(E\) satisfying \(E(N)\to0\) and
\[
\max\{e_{\mathrm{loc},n},e_{\mathrm{shell},n},
e_{\mathrm{zero},n},e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\}\le E(N)
\qquad(n\ge N).
\]
Consequently, for every rational \(\eta>0\), a terminating search returns a computable \(N^\dagger(\eta)\) such that, for all \(n\ge N^\dagger(\eta)\),
\[
d_n^-\le D_n\le d_n^+,
\qquad
|d_n^--\Lambda_{c^\dagger}|\le\eta,
\qquad
|D_n-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}|\le\eta,
\qquad
|d_n^+-\Lambda_{c^\dagger}|\le\eta.
\]
On the finite inadmissible prefix, the evaluator returns its flag and the deterministic zero estimator with the valid bracket \(0\le R_n(c^\dagger)\le1\); hence the finite-data procedure is total for every \(n\).  No computability representation of an arbitrary real contrast is used.
proposed.justification: The explicit error budget turns a limiting theorem into a finite, checkable claim and separates cross-sample convergence from action-grid discretization.
proposed.gap: The accepted parent bounds the two certificates at a selected \(n\) by \(1/(4G^2)\) but gives no computable threshold or allocation-shell modulus linking different population sizes.
proposed.consumer: A protocol designer can certify worst-case precision at a planned sample size from one prespecified sequence of tube widths, truncations, allocation radii, action grids, and rational enclosure widths.
